4-501.19
Temperature of wash solution in manual warewashing operation maintained at less than 43°C (110°F) or as otherwise specified.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: The temperature of the wash solution in manual warewashing equipment shall be maintained at not less than 43 degrees C (110 degrees F) or the temperature specified on the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today the kitchen and bar 3-comps were observed to be under 110F. The temperature of the wash solution in manual warewashing equipment shall be maintained at not less than 43°C (110°F) or the temperature specified on the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions. Correct within the week by contacting your hot water service provider.
6-301.11
Hand cleaning soap not available at each handwashing sink.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTIONCorrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Each handwashing sink or group of 2 adjacent handwashing sinks shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today a bar handsink was not supplied with soap. Each handwashing sink or group of 2 adjacent handwashing sinks shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. Thank you for restocking soap to this sink when this issue was brought to your attention. Correct within 3 days by re-educating staff on the importance of ensuring all handsinks are restocked once soap has run out.
3-307.11
Food not protected from all sources of contamination.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Food shall be protected from all sources of contamination.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today an ice scoop was observed to be resting in the ice machine's ice. Food shall be protected from all sources of contamination. Correct today by ensuring there is a clean, food-safe storage bin for the ice scoop and correct within three days by re-educating staff on proper prevention of contamination.
5-205.11
Handwashing sink used for purposes other than handwashing.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today a watering bucket was observed in a handwashing sink. A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. Correct by re-educating staff within one week on proper use of handsinks.
3-501.18
Ready-to eat time/temperature control for safety food not discarded when required.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food shall be discarded if it: exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or is appropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A).
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today several food items that were past their discard date such as cheese (10/28), sausage(10/22), garlic oil(11/7), and bloody mix (10/17) were observed. Ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food shall be discarded if it: exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or is appropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A). Correct today by discarding all expired TCS products and correct within three days by re-educating staff on proper TCS discarding procedure.
3-501.17
Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety food improperly date marked.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5 degrees C (41 degrees F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. The day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today a container of defrosting caramelized garlic was observed in the fridge with an august prep date. Food that is taken out of the freezer must be dated the day they were extracted from the freezer. Ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5°C (41°F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. The day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date. Correct by re-educating staff and ensuring all frozen items taken out of the freezer have the date they were taken out recorded.
4-501.114
Quaternary ammonium solution maintained at improper concentration.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Quaternary ammonium solution used for sanitizing shall be maintained per manufacturers instructions.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today one of the sani buckets in the kitchen concentration was observed to be 100ppm. Quaternary ammonium solution used for sanitizing shall be maintained per manufacturers instructions. This is a repeat violation. Correct by re-educating staff and ensuring buckets are maintained at 200-400ppm
3-302.11
Cross-contamination with raw animal products not adequately prevented in storage, preparation, holding, and display.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: All foods must be stored or prepared according to the final required minimum cooking temperature. In temperature (low to high) order this would be: cooked and ready-to-eat foods; followed by raw eggs and whole muscle fish and meats; followed by ground and injected fish and meats; followed by raw whole and ground poultry.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today a stack of cartons of raw eggs were observed to be sitting besides ready-to-eat cheese in the kitchen reach in, and raw eggs stored above the syrups at the bar. All foods must be stored or prepared according to the final required minimum cooking temperature. In temperature (low to high) order this would be: cooked and ready-to-eat foods; followed by raw eggs and whole muscle fish and meats; followed by ground and injected fish and meats; followed by raw whole and ground poultry. Correct today by reorganizing these reach-ins so that they have proper storage profiles, and correct within 3 days by re-educating staff on proper storage profiles.
5-103.11
Hot water capacity not sufficient to meet the peak needs of the establishment.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the food establishment.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Today there was no hot water at the beginning of the inspection. During the first round of water temp taking, all of the observed measurements were under 100F. After an hour of operation the water temps were retaken, and the handsinks were observed above 100F but the 3-comps were observed to still be below 110F. This is a repeat violation. Ensure you have hot water of at least 100F before opening.
